Appearance:
 Shri Rambihari Gautam - Advocate for the petitioner.
 Shri Vineet Singh - G.A. for the State.

Ms. Pushpanjaly Dwivedi - Advocate for the complainan
 Order

This Second bail application under Section 483 of BNS of 2023 for grant of bail has been filed on behalf of the applicant who has been arrested on 02.09.2025 in connection with Crime No.
127/2019 registered at Police Station N.K.J. District Katni for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) of I.P.C. and Sections 3 & 4 of POCSO Act.

2. It is argued by learned counsel for the applicant that first application was withdrawn on 27.09.2025 with liberty to repeat after statement of the prosecutrix and the statements of the prosecutrix has been recorded and the prosecutrix has turned hostile.

It is submitted that as per prosecution version the prosecutrix absconded on 25.09.2019 and the present applicant is stated to have taken away the prosecutrix and the said prosecutrix was then recovered on 16.08.2019.
Medical examination was conducted on 2 MCRC-47917-2025 16.08.2019 itself and vaginal slide as well as pubic hair and underwear were seized by the Medical Officer.
In the DNA examination report, no male chromosome has been detected in vaginal slide and in the pubic hair.
Only uninterpretable Y chromosome has been detected on underwear.
However, the profile was not sufficient for matching with the DNA sample of the present applicant.

3. It is further argued that though the prosecutrix is stated to be around 14 years of age, the present applicant is stated to be taken away the prosecutrix, but in her own statement before the trial Court she has stated that she was around 18 to 19 years of age at that time and also denied any act being committed with her by the present applicant.
Prayer is made to allow the application of bail.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent-State opposes the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the application.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the documents.

sentences.text: 6 . Considering the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, but without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is inclined to to grant bail to the applicant but with some stringent conditions.

It is hereby directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with One solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned.

7. This order shall remain operative subject to compliance of 3 MCRC-47917-2025 following stringent conditions by the applicant,:-
a.
The applicant will comply with all the terms and conditions of the bond executed by him;

b. The applicant will not indulge himself in extending inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to the Police Officer, as the case may be.
c. The applicant will cooperate in the trial and he shall not commit an of offence similar to the of offence of which he is accused;
d. The applicant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial;
e. The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Of icer, as the case may be; f.
The applicant shall not involve himself in any criminal activity in future otherwise, benefit of bail shall immediately be withdrawn.
g. In case of bail jump, this order shall become ineffective.
8. Application stands allowed and disposed of.
9. A copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance and information.
